Hi Jason —

Appreciate the context. Weve had similar asks for regulated customers and have a couple of pattern options wed like you to consider. High-level options (we can pick one during the call):

1) Strongly separated VPCs: control plane in a management VPC with private peering to the data plane; explicit NAT and egress proxies for the control plane only.
2) Shared fabric with strict ACLs: single VPC with microsegmented subnets and enforcement via an egress gateway (useful when the customer prefers minimized peerings).
3) Fully on-prem data plane + cloud-managed control plane: data plane sits in Nebulas edge/colo, with mTLS tunnels to the control plane.

Quick asks from our side to make the sketch useful: expected sustained inference throughput (rps / tokens/sec), whether you need outbound-only egress or inbound model updates, and whether theres an existing BGP relationship for cross-site routing.

Im attaching our starter runbook (redwood-private-deploy-runbook-v1.docx) to outline pilot steps, required inventory, and the rollback plan. If you can populate the inventory (Priya), well produce a topology diagram and a recommended firewall/ACL matrix.

Proposed next steps:
- Priya to share the filled inventory by Fri (7/6)
- 30-min tech sync w/ Redwood infra + Nebula network (pick Mon/Tue 7/8-7/9)
- Produce reference diagrams and checklist for pilot (deliver by 7/13)

If those dates work Ill book a slot.

Best,

Adding a technical checklist from the runtime/operator perspective — copying Soojin who will own the observability/egress details:

Adityas quick checklist for topology and controls:

A) Control / Data plane boundary
- Prefer explicit management VPC for control plane components (control plane API servers, job schedulers, telemetry collectors).
- Data plane (inference nodes) deployed in a customer-managed VPC/subnets or on-prem rack; avoid shared storage endpoints that cross the boundary.

B) Networking and routing
- If peering is used, enforce route filters so the management VPC does not advertise customer-specific subnets.
- BGP: use an MD5-protected BGP session if youre peering to an on-prem BGP speaker; otherwise use static tunnel routes.
- Egress proxy: recommended for control plane outbound calls (for updates, metrics) — allows IP allowlisting on Nebula side.

C) Security and encryption
- mTLS for all control plane <> data plane gRPC channels; cert rotation via your KMS/HSM is preferred.
- Per-tenant encryption keys for logs and artifacts if Nebula requires separation.

D) Observability and circuit breakers
- Separate telemetry streams (control-plane metrics vs. inference metrics) with distinct retention policies.
- Implement rate-limited canary rollouts: small percentage of traffic routed to new model variants, automated rollback on error budget breach.

E) Operational runbook items (pilot scope)
- Pilot: 2 Availability Zones, single customer topology, synthetic load test (10k tokens/min), failover exercise with 30% AZ outage.
- Cutover: staged DNS shift + traffic fencing via feature flags.

Im attaching a diagram draft and a control-data boundary checklist for your network team to review.

[Attachment: control-data-boundary-draft.pdf (pdf, 196 KB)]

Let us know if Nebula policy requires that control plane logs never transit the public internet (we can accommodate via private peering + VPC endpoints).

-Aditya
